CONDITIONAL

**Scope.** I checked the diff (`c6be53b..HEAD`, `emotion-accumulation-paper/main.tex`) against primary sources:
- both `.tex` editions;
- page 1 of both rebuilt PDFs, viewed directly;
- `data/accumulation_results.json`, `data/accumulation_controls.json` and `data/dose_response_results.json`, read directly;
- `code/dose_response_accumulation.py` lines 140–179;
- the six review JSONs and `REMEDIATION_REGISTER.md`.

Every new number in the abstract matches the shipped data: +4.75/+4.22 → +0.44/−0.34; gaps 0.53–0.78; 59/135 and 54/135; d_av −0.68; minimum permutation p 0.063. The twin edition carries the same new text. Both PDFs show the reframe on page 1. All six review artifacts exist: r1, r2 and r3 dated 2026‑11‑02 UTC, and r4_ea, r5_ea and r6_ea dated 2026‑11‑08 UTC. In US Pacific time that is 11‑01 to 11‑07, which matches the claim.

## Findings

**1. MAJOR: "the one length-matched comparison" is false, and the shipped data hold a matched comparison that answers more directly.**
- **Where:** `main.tex:78`, `:170`, `:911` and header `:12`; `academic/main.tex` at the same lines; `paper.json` abstract.
- **Primary data (`accumulation_results.json`):** initial-study travel prompt lengths are cheerful 363, 363, 320 and hostile 363, 311, 363. The 320 and 311 reruns are the two whose planning the chat template stripped (r6 `f1_initial_think_trials`). The other four, two per arm, are all exactly 363 tokens.
- **What that means:** this is a cheerful-vs-hostile *history* comparison with the same neutral probe at the same position. Its gap is the +0.08 the body already reports at `:271` (SDs 0.23 and 0.12; r6 `x_initial_topic_gaps_excl_stripped`). The body never calls it length-matched. The body sentence "differ by 4–7 tokens in four of the five topics" (`:276`) is accurate but leaves out that the fifth topic is matched.
- **Effect on the argument:** the Introduction's "three reasons" (`:153–165`) don't explain why this sub-comparison can't test accumulation, since position is matched there. The real reasons are: one topic, two reruns of one script, an undocumented read site, and planning text in the history.
- **Fix:**
  - Reword to "the one comparison length-matched on every probe".
  - Add one sentence in the abstract, Introduction and Conclusion. In the initial study's travel topic, two reruns per arm are length-matched at 363 tokens. Their gap at the probe is +0.08 against rerun SDs of 0.23 and 0.12. That is one topic and one script, too few to test anything, and the read site is undocumented.
  - Update `paper.json` and both editions.

**2. MAJOR: the prescribed control "position-matched *or* de-rotated keys" does not control what the paper says it controls.**
- **Where:** abstract `:83`, §7 item 3 (`:863–870`), Conclusion `:918`.
- **Problem (a), the directions:** the compass concatenates *cached* keys, which are post-RoPE, across four layers × four KV heads × 256 dimensions and dot-products them with the directions (`dose_response_accumulation.py:150–174`). The directions were also built from cached, post-RoPE story keys. If only the read keys are de-rotated, they get projected onto directions whose rotated part was never de-rotated. That frame mismatch adds its own position-dependent error.
- **Problem (b), history:** de-rotation removes only the rotary channel. The pre-RoPE key at layer 3 still depends on how many tokens came before it, and on what they said, through linear-attention layers 0–2. That is "the amount of history", which the paper's own headline says is not separated from position. Without length matching, cheerful and hostile histories of different lengths stay confounded even after de-rotation.
- **Fix:** require position and length matching in every case. Keep de-rotation only as an extra diagnostic, and only with the directions rebuilt from de-rotated calibration keys. Change the "or" in all three places.

**3. MINOR: the abstract's example of position/history drift uses a quantity whose make-up changes with dose.**
- **Where:** `:68–71`.
- **Problem:** the chunk average covers 2 chunks at dose 1 and 9 at dose 8. Half of the dose‑1 average is chunk 0, which comes before any history and reads 4.85 (cheerful) and 3.77 (hostile). The body notes this at `:402`; the abstract doesn't.
- **Fix:** use the probe-chunk numbers instead. The probe text is the same at every dose, and it reads 4.61/4.65 at dose 1, −1.75/−1.90 at dose 4 and −1.60/−3.71 at dose 8 (r5 `f2`). Note that this chunk also holds the tail of the previous generated turn. Alternatively, add "(the average covers 2 chunks at dose 1, 9 at dose 8)".

**4. MINOR: the planning-text reason is stated more broadly than its evidence.**
- **Where:** Introduction `:158–161`, Conclusion `:896–899`, abstract `:72–75`.
- **Problem:** these say "the stored assistant turns in the histories are planning text" without saying which experiments. Experiment 2 stored no response text (`:295`), so for Experiment 2 this cannot be checked.
- **Two smaller issues:**
  - The stored turns are 100-character excerpts of 60-token turns. "Open with planning", as the body says at `:323`, is the supported claim; "are planning text" is not.
  - At least one of the 54 cheerful hits does not name the user's tone: `dose_response_results.json:4208`, "Problem: I'm glad you're getting inspired".
- **Fix:** say this applies to Experiment 1 and the initial study only. Say "open with planning". Say "use a tone word, almost always describing the user".

**5. MINOR: the Experiment 3 caveat in the abstract and Conclusion is incomplete.**
- **Problem:** both say "its script is not shipped" but not that its read site is undocumented (`:527–535`). The standard the paper used to withdraw Experiment 2 needs identical text at the read site. If Experiment 3 reads the system-prompt tokens, its arms differ in text there.
- **Partial evidence:** the controls file stores `logit_entropy` and `logit_margin`, which fits a read at the last position. It does not document where the keys were read.
- **Fix:** add "and its read site is undocumented" in both places.

**6. MINOR: the correction note is now out of date.**
- **Where:** `:186–187`.
- **Problem:** it says the abstract now "state[s] what the cited work supports, and give[s] each number its own result against text". After the reframe, the abstract says nothing about the cited work.
- **Fix:** "Since 2026‑11‑08 the abstract no longer cites the single-turn results; the Introduction's first paragraph states what they support."

**7. MINOR: weather/climate wording survives the retitle.**
- **Where:** Discussion `:591–616`; Limitations item 15 in the flight edition, item 16 in the academic edition.
- **Problem:** both still present "weather not climate" as the paper's own framing. The Discussion also keeps the hypothesis "the system prompt may act as a climate setting", which rests only on Experiment 3. The Retitled note says only the Discussion *heading* was reworded.
- **Fix:** label the Limitations item "The former 'weather not climate' framing", and cut or explicitly mark that hypothesis.

**8. MINOR: §7 item 2 can't be carried out as written.**
- **Problem:** reading the 48 linear-attention layers' state needs emotion directions in that state's space. That state is a matrix per head, not a vector in key space, and the calibration routine (`decision_moment.py` `calibrate`) only builds key-space directions for the full-attention layers.
- **Fix:** name the calibration step. Also, "would need" overstates: a test of whether *these keys* accumulate doesn't require the recurrent layers.

**9. MINOR (pre-existing twin desync).** "Conversation-level clustering" is commented out in the flight edition (`main.tex:797–806`) but live in the academic edition (`academic/main.tex:782–790`), so the two Limitations lists differ in length. The items the new text cites (2, 5, 6, 9, 14) mean the same thing in both editions, so the diff doesn't make this worse.

**Known kills:**
- **Label without its statistic:** finding 1, plus finding 3.
- **Unresolved review flag:** register row N2 (lyra-technique-ii is uncorrected) is still OPEN. The paper discloses this at `:109` and takes its numbers from the user-model paper only. Not triggered.
- **Claimed review not run:** six artifacts exist. Not triggered.
- **Prose-only claim:** the new numbers trace to shipped r5/r6 output. But "the one length-matched comparison" is a prose-only claim that the shipped data contradict (finding 1).
- **Double-counted experiment:** Experiment 3's no-history arm is bit-identical to the initial study's. This is disclosed, and nothing is counted twice in any tally. Not triggered.
- **Outcome-informed taxonomy:** the tone-word rules were written after seeing the data. Each of the three revisions lowered the count (cheerful 69 → 67 → 54), and the zeros across arms don't depend on the rules. Not triggered.
- **Architecture vs config:** 16 full-attention layers at 3, 7, …, 63, plus 48 linear-attention layers. Partial rotary factor 0.25 gives 64 of 256 dimensions rotated. `DynamicCache` builds one entry per model layer (`decision-state-paper/data/r5_transformers_key_cache_order.json`), so `cache.layers[3,7,11,15]` are model layers 3, 7, 11 and 15. Not triggered.

## What I could NOT check

- **Script runs:** running `python tools/verify_pdf.py` needed approval I didn't have. I checked PDF page 1 of both editions visually, and grepped `academic/main.txt`. Body pages of the PDFs are **UNVERIFIED**.
- **Edition diff:** I couldn't mechanically diff the two editions (`git diff --no-index` needed approval). I grepped every new string and read the academic Limitations, §7 and Conclusion in full.
- **Read sites:** the initial study's and Experiment 3's read sites are unknown; their scripts are not shipped. Finding 1's "same position" assumes the probe is read at the probe, as the paper says.
- **Transformers version:** the version used for the runs is not recorded, so cache indexing is confirmed only for 5.3.0 and 5.22.2. I could not read the installed library, which is outside the allowed directories.
- **Model config:** the config r5 checked comes from the Hugging Face hub. Whether it belongs to the distill or the base model is not stated.
- **The +0.08:** I didn't recompute it from raw projections. I took it from r6 and the body. Which four trials it covers I verified from the primary `prompt_len` values.
- **Correction note history:** I couldn't trace where the note's "second paragraph of this Introduction" came from (a piped `git show` needed approval). The upstream user-model numbers are unchanged by this diff and were not re-audited.

AGNI-VERDICT: CONDITIONAL
